info.name: GenLink KH — Backend API
info.description:
GenLink KH backend (Spring Boot, port 8888).

## Quick start
1. Set the `baseUrl` variable if your server is not on http://localhost:8888.
2. Run **Auth > Register**, then **Auth > Verify Email** with the 6-digit OTP.
   The OTP is printed to the backend console (`EMAIL OTP FOR ...`), which is handy
   because SMTP may not be configured.
3. Or just run **Auth > Login** if you already have an account.

Login, Verify Email, Verify OTP and the Refresh requests all capture
`accessToken` and `refreshToken` into collection variables automatically, so
every other request is authenticated for you.

## Notes
- All responses are wrapped: `{ success, message, data, errorCode, timestamp }`.
- Auth is Bearer JWT, set once at collection level. Public endpoints override it to none.
- Access tokens last 15 minutes and carry a `tv` (token version) claim. Logout,
  change-password and revoke-all bump it, so the token dies immediately — that is
  intended, just log in again.
- `Accept-Language: km` or `en` controls the language of system content such as
  interest names. Default is Khmer.

exec: // Nothing global yet. Token capture lives on the auth requests.

Creates the account as PENDING and sends an OTP.
Set {{otp}} to the 6 digits from the backend console first. Activates the account and returns tokens.
Rate limited: 5 failures per 15 min, then a 15 min block (AUTH_TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS).

Send a GOOGLE ID token from google_sign_in — not a Firebase ID token.
Verified against Google's public keys using app.google.client-id, so GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID must be set on the server.
Hard to exercise from Postman; easiest from the Flutter client.
Deliberately does not reveal whether the account exists — an unknown email returns the same message.
Same behaviour as Resend OTP; this is the hardened implementation the other one delegates to.
Rotates the refresh token. Reusing an old one is detected (TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED). /auth/refresh-token is an alias.
Revokes refresh tokens AND bumps token_version, so the current access token stops working immediately. Expect 401 on the next authenticated request until you log in again.

item.name: Saved Items
item.description:
One saved list across every domain, backed by saved_items.

Rows are hydrated: each carries title, subtitle, imageUrl and `available`, so the Saved screen renders from ONE call instead of one fetch per item.

`available: false` means the saved thing was deleted — item_id is not a foreign key because the table is polymorphic. Show a 'no longer available' row rather than a blank one.

request.description:
Newest first, hydrated. Add ?type=POST to filter.

Titles of system content (MOTIVATION, LESSON, SHORT_CONTENT) follow Accept-Language.
Lookups are batched per type, so a 50-item list is ~7 queries, not 50.

request.description:
itemType: POST | DISCUSSION | EVENT | OPPORTUNITY | MOTIVATION | LESSON | SHORT_CONTENT

Idempotent: saving twice returns the existing row instead of failing on the unique constraint.

itemId is not a foreign key (the table is polymorphic), so no check is made that the target exists.
For rendering the save toggle without fetching the whole list. Returns { saved: true|false }.

item.description: Profile domain: own profile, settings, interests, portfolio, social links, saved items.

request.description:
Revokes every session and bumps token_version, so your current token dies immediately — log in again afterwards.
Rate limited: 5 failures per 15 min, then a 15 min block.
Google-only accounts get AUTH_PASSWORD_NOT_SET.
Live sign-ins with device, IP and last-used. Token hashes are never exposed.

Known limitation: revokes that device's refresh token, but its existing access token still works until it expires (max 15 min). Token versioning is per-user, so bumping it would sign out every device.
Immediate: bumps token_version, so all access tokens die at once — including this one.
Last 50 security events: logins, failures, password changes, session revokes.

item.name: Events & RSVP
item.description: Events with capacity and simulated paid entry via the demo wallet. Capacity is checked before payment.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Flutter Workshop",
  "description": "Intro to Flutter",
  "category": "WORKSHOP",
  "coverImageUrl": null,
  "dateTime": "2026-08-01T14:00:00",
  "locationName": "ACLEDA University",
  "attendeeLimit": 50,
  "status": "PUBLISHED",
  "language": "ENGLISH",
  "paid": false,
  "price": null
}

request.description:
status: DRAFT | PUBLISHED | CANCELLED | COMPLETED
dateTime is a local date-time (no offset).

paid + price: a paid event MUST have a price above zero (chk_events_paid_requires_price).
Payment is SIMULATED against the demo wallet - there is no real KHQR transfer.
Events you organise, including drafts. Paginated.

Published upcoming events, soonest first. Add ?category=WORKSHOP to filter.

Past events and DRAFTs are excluded. Rows carry organizer, myRsvpStatus and full, so the list renders Join/Cancel without extra calls.

Idempotent - RSVPing twice does not double-count or re-award XP.

Order matters: capacity is checked BEFORE payment, so a full paid event never charges you.

Free event -> joins, +10 XP.
Paid event -> deducts the demo wallet, writes a demo_transaction (EVENT_PAYMENT), returns amountPaid and simulatedPayment=true. Label it a simulation on screen.

Errors: EVENT_FULL, EVENT_CANCELLED, EVENT_PAST, DEMO_WALLET_NOT_FOUND, DEMO_WALLET_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE.
No refund: the demo wallet has no refund flow.

request.description:
anonymous=true hides the author in every response.

The author id is still STORED on the row for moderation - it is withheld at the DTO boundary, not discarded. Commenters are never anonymous; only the discussion author is.
Your own discussions, including ones you posted anonymously. Paginated.

The forum list, newest first. Add ?category=TECH to filter.

Anonymous rows come back with author = null. reactedByMe and mine are resolved server-side.
Idempotent. forum_reactions has UNIQUE(discussion_id, user_id), so a double tap returns the same count. Returns {reactionCount}.

One report per user per discussion, so report_count means distinct people, not taps.
Reporting twice is a silent no-op.

NOTE: nothing reviews the report queue yet - there is no moderation screen. Reports land in discussion_reports and a log line.
Forum comments are flat - parentCommentId is ignored here (forum_comments has no parent column). Threading exists on post comments only.
Oldest first, so a thread reads top to bottom. Commenters are always identified.

item.name: Mobile (BFF-lite)
item.description: Aggregation endpoints for dashboard-heavy screens. Capped at 5-6 by design.

request.description:
Home Super Dashboard - every card in one call.

Returns: user, todayProgress (habits + tasks), dailyChallenge, financeSnapshot (budget + savings), upcomingEvent, recommendedCommunities, dailyMotivation, feedPreview.

Cards are NULLABLE by design: a new user has no budget, no RSVP and maybe no challenge. null means 'render this card's empty state', not an error. Lists are empty, never null.

Titles of system content (challenge, motivation) follow Accept-Language.

Daily motivation rotates by day-of-year, so it is stable across refreshes.
